BAKERY PRODUCTION SCHEDULER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

What time do you have to start baking?

List your products (batch size, prep, proof and bake minutes, price and cost) and your orders with due times. The scheduler works backwards from each due time, shares your ovens and bakers across the whole morning, and tells you when the first person has to start, whether that is before you open, what extra oven or baker fixes it, and which orders to turn down if nothing can be added.

Planning arithmetic on your own numbers and stated assumptions.

1. Your shop

2. Products

One per line: name, units per batch, prep min, proof min, bake min, unit price, unit cost. Lines starting with # are ignored.

3. Orders

One per line: customer or label, product, quantity, due time.

Result

Questions people ask

How do I schedule baking backwards from a delivery time?

Take the due time, subtract the cooling gap, then subtract bake time, proof time and prep time in that order. That is the latest each step can start. This tool does it for every batch at once and then slides batches earlier only when an oven or a baker is already busy.

How many ovens and bakers does my order list need?

It depends on the due times, not the total volume. Enter your orders and the tool tries more ovens and bakers until the earliest prep start falls after your shop opens, and tells you the smallest addition that works.

What if the orders do not fit?

The tool ranks orders by profit per oven hour and shows which to turn down so the rest fits, keeping any smaller order that still squeezes in.

Is this business advice?

No. It is scheduling arithmetic on the numbers you type in. Check the timeline against your real equipment, recipes and food-safety rules before you rely on it.

Not decided

Oven temperatures and steam (every batch is assumed to fit any oven slot at any time), mixer and bench space, staff breaks and pay, delivery driving time, shelf life, ingredient stock, allergen separation and food-safety rules. Every batch is a whole batch, so unsold leftovers carry cost and no revenue. Prep is assumed to be one baker for the full prep time.

Pricing a baked good for a wholesale account first? The cottage food pricing calculator and the Faire wholesale calculator work out price from cost. Renting kitchen time? The shared kitchen rate planner.

Deciding how many to make rather than when? The daily prep quantity optimizer picks the profit-maximising batch count from your past daily sales.

Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (plan_run, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.
